concepts.definition: The keys the player uses to run the game: four direction keys and the A and B buttons.
concepts.example: On a keyboard the arrows and Space act as the controller; on a phone the on-screen keys under the stage do.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking you cannot play with keys on a touch screen; there is an on-screen version of the same keys under the stage.

concepts.definition: The number that tells you how many pixels a sprite goes in one second.
concepts.example: If the speed is 60, the cat walks 120 pixels in 2 seconds while the key is held down.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing a speed that is too big; at values like 200 the cat goes too fast to control.

concepts.definition: The choice in the key movement block that decides which keys work: in 4 directions, left-right or up-down.
concepts.example: If you set the fruit basket to left-right, the up and down keys do not move the basket.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking it is a bug that the up key does not work while left-right is chosen; it is the rule of the way you chose.

concepts.definition: The setting that stops a sprite at the edge of the stage.
concepts.example: With this setting on, holding the left key down for a long time stops the cat at the left edge.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to add the setting; the sprite leaves the screen and cannot be seen, but it stays in the game.

concepts.definition: One step of the game, repeated 60 times a second; in every frame the keys are checked and the sprites are moved.
concepts.example: While the right key is held down, the cat slides right by one sixtieth of its speed in every frame.
concepts.pitfall: Trying to build a loop to keep running the movement block; the key movement block runs once and stays in force for the whole game.

quiz.prompt: You are making a fruit basket at the bottom of the screen that only slides right and left. Which way of moving should you choose?
options: None; the basket cannot move with keys
quiz.explanation: The left-right way only responds to the left and right keys; the basket does not go up by mistake. If you choose in 4 directions, the up and down keys move the basket too. Up-down does the exact opposite.

quiz.prompt: The cat is standing at x 80. Its movement speed is 60 and the stay on screen setting is off. If you hold the right key down for exactly 2.5 seconds, how many pixels does the cat travel?
quiz.explanation: Distance = speed x time = 60 x 2.5 = 150 pixels. Stay on screen is off, so the cat goes all the way to x 230, outside the stage. If the setting were on, it would stop at the right edge.

quiz.prompt:
The player holds the up key down for 1 second. What does the cat do?

```
when game starts
  kedi = new Cat sprite, kind Player
  move kedi to x 80 y 60
  kedi moves left-right with player keys, speed 60
```
options: The game gives an error and stops
quiz.explanation: The left-right way only listens to the left and right keys. The up key does nothing with this way; it does not give an error either. For it to go up, in 4 directions or up-down should have been chosen.

quiz.prompt:
When you press the arrow keys, the cat does not move at all. What is the bug?

```
when game starts
  kedi = new Cat sprite, kind Player
  move kedi to x 80 y 60

kedi moves in 4 directions with player keys, speed 60
```
options: The movement block is not attached inside the when game starts block, so it never runs
Left-right should be chosen instead of in 4 directions
quiz.explanation: Blocks only run if they are connected to an event block. The movement block is on the loose line at the bottom, outside the when game starts block. The speed value and the position are not the problem; in 4 directions already listens to all the keys.

quiz.prompt: Without the stay on screen setting, the cat went out through the left edge. What happens to the cat?
options: It is deleted from the game
It comes back in through the right edge
It cannot be seen, but it stays in the game
quiz.explanation: When a sprite leaves the screen it is not deleted; it just cannot be seen and it is still in the game. It does not come back by itself through another edge, and it does not stop the game. To keep it on the stage, you turn on the stay on screen setting.
